title: Reinhart and Rogoff public debt and growth panel (Herndon-Ash-Pollin 2014 replication columns)

Downloaded from PERI's replication page (RR-keycolumns.xlsx), which the authors post for free reuse. The original Reinhart-Rogoff site (reinhartandrogoff.com, scholar.harvard.edu/rogoff) returned 403/blocked responses when checked; see todo-reports/finance.md.

title: Nakamura and Steinsson (2018) monetary policy news shock
variables: date, policy_news_shock, ffr_shock
notes: One row per FOMC announcement, Jan 2000-Mar 2014 (excludes unscheduled meetings and the Sep 2008-Jun 2009 financial-crisis window). policy_news_shock is the first principal component of five interest-rate futures in a 30-minute window, rescaled to match the 1-year nominal Treasury yield response; ffr_shock is the unexpected change in the fed funds rate. Author's site, no licence stated. A SOFR-futures update by Acosta, Brennan and Jacobson (2024) exists on Harvard Dataverse but is CC BY-NC and not redistributable here.

title: Nakamura and Steinsson (2018) monetary policy news shock, extended sample
variables: date, unscheduled, policy_news_shock, ffr_shock
notes: Same construction as ns2018 but Jan 1995-Mar 2014, including unscheduled meetings (flagged by unscheduled) and the financial crisis window (excludes the two Sep 2001 meetings). The policy news shock differs slightly from ns2018 on overlapping dates because it is re-estimated on the larger sample.

title: Swanson (2021) FFR, forward guidance and LSAP factors
variables: date, ff_factor, fg_factor, lsap_factor
notes: One row per FOMC announcement, Jul 1991-Jun 2019: three orthogonal factors (fed funds, forward guidance, large-scale asset purchases) extending Gurkaynak-Sack-Swanson (2005) through the ZLB and QE period. Author's site, no licence stated.

See bs2023_fomc for the announcement-level data and control variables. Snapshot from the SF Fed data page, 2026-09.

title: Bauer and Swanson (2023) monetary policy surprises, FOMC-announcement level
variables: date, time, unscheduled, ff1, ff2, ed1, ed2, ed3, ed4, sp500, sp500_emini, tnote02, tnote05, tnote10, tbond, mps, mps_orth, nfp_surp, nfp_12m, sp500_3m, slope_3m, bcom_3m, tr_skew
notes: One row per FOMC announcement, Feb 1988-Dec 2023: fed funds and Eurodollar futures (ff1-ff2, ed1-ed4), Treasury note/bond yields, S&P 500, MPS and MPS_ORTH plus the pre-FOMC control surprises (payrolls, S&P momentum, yield-curve slope, commodities, Treasury option skew) used to orthogonalise MPS. Updates the original Gurkaynak-Sack-Swanson/Swanson-Jayawickrema series; maintained by the SF Fed.

title: Miranda-Agrippino and Ricco (2021) informationally-robust monetary policy instrument
variables: date, fomc_date, gb_date, is_fomc, is_unscheduled, iv1, iv5
notes: One row per FOMC date, Feb 1990-Dec 2009 (fomc_date and gb_date give the meeting and preceding Greenbook publication date). is_unscheduled flags non-scheduled meetings; iv1/iv5 are the fed funds futures (FF4) instruments purged of Fed information effects, built at all Greenbook rounds (iv1) and at scheduled FOMC only (iv5). Author's site, no licence stated.

title: Kanzig (2021) oil supply news shocks
variables: date, oil_supply_surprise, oil_supply_news_shock
notes: Monthly 1975-01 to 2025-12: the oil supply surprise (change in the front-month Brent futures price around OPEC announcements) and the oil supply news shock extracted from the paper's VAR. title: Baumeister and Hamilton (2019) structural oil supply and demand shocks
variables: date, supply_shock, activity_shock, consumption_demand_shock, inventory_demand_shock
notes: Monthly 1975-02 to 2026-03 posterior-median structural shocks from the incomplete-identification oil SVAR: supply_shock, activity_shock (global economic activity), consumption_demand_shock and inventory_demand_shock. Author's site, updated periodically; snapshot 2026-09.

title: Lettau and Ludvigson (2001) consumption-wealth ratio (cay)

notes: Quarterly 1952Q1-2019Q3: log consumption (c), log asset wealth (w), log labour income (y) and the cointegrating residual cay = c - 0.218 w - 0.801 y + 0.441. From 2014Q3 the authors construct consumption from PCE rather than nondurables-and-services. Hosted on Martin Lettau's site (sydneyludvigson.com posts the appendix only); no licence stated; not updated past 2019Q3 as of this snapshot.
